name: Fjaðrárgljúfur canyon rim
why: Up the edge of a twisting gorge 100 m deep and 2 km long, cut into two-million-year-old palagonite, from viewpoint to viewpoint to a waterfall at the top.
book: No permit. Road 206 off Route 1 west of Kirkjubæjarklaustur; small cars can drive it all year. The Environment Agency has closed the path for weeks in thaw (2018 and 2019, reopened on 1 June): check Safetravel or the local information before you go.
water: Toilets at the car park; no water on the path. Kirkjubæjarklaustur has shops.
dangers: Unfenced cliff edges: stay behind the ropes and on the platforms.
Ice on the path in winter and deep mud in the spring thaw; walking off the path destroys the moss and is why the canyon gets closed.
turnaround: At the upper platform by Mögárfoss: the path ends there. Walking into the canyon bed means wading in the river.

points.name: Fjaðrá river mouth car park
points.note: Where the Fjaðrá leaves the canyon onto the plain. From the car park a short path goes to the river at the canyon mouth; the rim path climbs to the right.

points.name: Middle viewpoint on the east rim
points.note: A platform over the narrowest bends: sheer walls of moss and rock with the river far below.

points.name: Fjaðrárgljúfur upper lookout
points.note: The steel platform at the end of the path, looking down the whole canyon. Mögárfoss falls down the opposite wall. Back the same way.
